nodes.label: Negative counting-down ids for locally synthesized entries
nodes.rationale: Locally synthesized system entries (/help, /sheet, 'Saved.') use a counter that decrements from 0 so they can never collide with the controller's own positive, incrementing StoryEntry ids.

nodes.label: Terminal drops 'roll' story entries
nodes.rationale: The TUI has an always-mounted DiceLine card, so letting 'roll' entries into the log too would print every roll twice; the web client has no such card and renders rolls inline instead.

nodes.label: All game state reaches React only through ControllerCallbacks
nodes.rationale: App never reaches into the engine/DM session directly, and slash commands are parsed in the UI layer so GameController stays UI-free -- which is exactly what lets the web bridge reuse it unmodified.

nodes.label: Fallback-message echo suppression by content
nodes.rationale: onDiceRoll fires for every roll_dice call including the one just handled interactively, and its text is identical to reveal.message; recognizing the echo BY CONTENT rather than by timing keeps the compact summary on screen, because two independently-scheduled state updates give no guaranteed observable order.

nodes.label: Fixed 3-row dice card phase machine (idle/waiting/animating/revealed)
nodes.rationale: Merged the old DiceLine+RollPrompt into one always-mounted card so numbers always get their own row; a sentence-length DM `reason` once pushed the total/DC/success off the end of a single truncated line. Only the reason may truncate; numbers are composed from structured RollRevealResult fields, never parsed from a string.

nodes.label: Roll-pending input ownership handoff
nodes.rationale: While a player roll is pending, InputBar's whole key hook goes inactive and DiceLine owns the keyboard, so Esc is a total no-op and can never interrupt the DM turn mid-roll.

nodes.label: Only the focused option shows its description
nodes.rationale: Keeps a long list of richly-described options (classes/races/backgrounds) compact instead of printing every description at once.

nodes.label: Scroll anchoring: snap only on player entry or fresh stream
nodes.rationale: Snapping on every partial tick would fight a player scrolled up mid-stream rereading something, so only a new PLAYER entry or the start of a fresh DM stream yanks the view back to the bottom.

nodes.label: Whole-frame-height invariant
nodes.rationale: storyHeight + DICE_AREA_HEIGHT + INPUT_BAR_HEIGHT must always equal the terminal's rows exactly, which is what keeps the UI from ever spilling into terminal scrollback. The arithmetic is split out of App.tsx so tests can import it without ink/react.

nodes.label: Ink-free shared slash-command formatting
nodes.rationale: This module builds only plain strings so both front ends can share it unmodified; dispatch (which command maps to which controller call) lives in App.tsx for the TUI and src/web/server.ts for phone/web play. /retire and /quit are omitted from the web help because on web they are UI (a button, closing the tab), not typed commands.

nodes.label: Per (entry id, width) wrap memoization
nodes.rationale: Streaming re-renders every ~80ms would otherwise re-wrap the whole scrollback; the cache is a pure performance detail owned by the caller and never part of the result, so the function stays deterministic and unit-testable without React/ink.

nodes.label: Universal raw-mode gate for every input hook
nodes.rationale: Under non-TTY stdin (piped, --render-check, CI) ink's setRawMode throws and takes down the whole render; isRawModeSupported is `undefined` rather than `false` there and ink guards with a strict === false check, so the value must be coerced to a real boolean.

nodes.label: Retire mode reuses the creation wizard
nodes.rationale: /retire runs the same wizard with mode 'retire': the world already exists, so campaign-name/theme/content-rating are skipped and it collects only a fresh hero for the same persistent campaign/world/chronicle. The confirm screen shows base vs post-race stats side by side so the player sees exactly what their race added.

nodes.label: Transient vs mirrored SSE events
nodes.rationale: 'note' and 'ledger' are session-level toasts, never stored, so a reconnect never replays a stale one. Suggestions ARE mirrored because chips belong to the scene on screen: a phone that locks mid-scene must get its chips back or the buttons vanish for the rest of the turn.

nodes.label: onDiceRoll deliberately does nothing on web
nodes.rationale: The roll already reaches the client as a 'roll' STORY ENTRY via onStoryAppend, in sequence, so it lands where it happened and stays there. Mirroring it into snapshot state as well is what used to leave the newest roll pinned under the input for turns after the scene had moved on.

nodes.label: Idempotent hello snapshot for phone reconnects
nodes.rationale: A phone's EventSource can reconnect at any point (screen lock, network blip), so every new client gets a full snapshot and must never assume continuity; state is deep-cloned (structuredClone) because the Engine mutates GameState in place.

nodes.label: env > --flag > default config precedence
nodes.rationale: A container/VM has no shell to pass --port to, so each of PORT/HOST/GAME_PIN/SAVES_DIR has a pure resolve*() with env precedence and a safe fallback. GAME_PIN matters most: a freshly generated per-boot PIN is useless once a host can restart the process without the owner watching the console.

nodes.label: An operator-supplied PIN is never echoed to the console
nodes.rationale: A generated PIN exists nowhere else so the console is the only place to learn it; a GAME_PIN was chosen by its operator and printing it copies a password into journald/`docker logs` for every boot in the retention window.

nodes.label: Plain http + SSE instead of WebSockets
nodes.rationale: Node's stdlib has `http` but no WS server and this project takes no new dependencies; SSE covers a turn-based game fine and gives reconnect-on-drop for free via the browser's EventSource -- exactly what a phone needs across screen locks and network blips.

nodes.label: Per-player session isolation via saveDir + own SSE sinks
nodes.rationale: Everything that used to be a module-scope singleton (bridge/controller/activeState) moved into a per-player Session keyed by playerId; each GameBridge owns its OWN sink set so a broadcast can never reach another player's stream, and loadGame is scoped to session.saveDir so another player's slug simply isn't found.

nodes.label: Single-use SSE tickets instead of credentials in URLs
nodes.rationale: EventSource cannot set headers, so /api/events historically took ?pin=. Query strings leak into reverse-proxy access logs, tunnel/CDN logs, browser history and Referer headers; a long-lived per-player access code there is worse because it never rotates. A ticket is deleted on first use and expires in 30s, so leaking one is worth nothing.

nodes.label: index.html served no-cache with a size+mtime ETag
nodes.rationale: The whole client is one file with no build hash to bust. With no cache headers a phone kept rendering the old numbers-only PIN field after the access-code login shipped, so no valid code could be typed; no-cache plus an ETag gives correctness without re-sending 240KB per load.

nodes.label: Five-screen state machine (title/pin/campaigns/wizard/play)
nodes.rationale: showScreen publishes the active screen on #app's dataset so CSS can vary the frame per screen; a stray hello reporting no campaign must never yank the player out of the pin, wizard or title screens.

nodes.label: submitPin
nodes.rationale: enterAfterAuth must be called explicitly here: the SSE hello handler deliberately never navigates away from the PIN screen, so without it a correct PIN validated server-side while the page stayed frozen (the launch-day phone bug).

nodes.label: applyAuthMode (shapes the single login field)
nodes.rationale: Defaults to the permissive 'code' mode so every path fails OPEN: a digits-only sanitiser left armed by a slow /api/auth-mode silently ate access codes as they were typed. 'none' (--no-pin) must skip the login screen entirely -- it previously demanded a 6-digit PIN that never existed.

nodes.label: enterAfterAuth (landing rule)
nodes.rationale: Someone with campaigns goes straight to their shelf -- the title card is a front door, not a toll gate paid on every visit; someone with nothing to resume gets the title card rather than an empty list.

nodes.label: confirmDeleteCampaign (inline confirm)
nodes.rationale: Confirmation replaces the card rather than opening a dialog, so the campaign being destroyed stays named and on screen while the player decides.

nodes.label: signOut
nodes.rationale: Deliberately does NOT end the server-side session: signing out is a client act, and killing a live game because someone handed the phone over would lose the turn in flight.

nodes.label: continueCampaign
nodes.rationale: A 409 'session already running' still routes to the play screen (attaching to the live session via SSE is exactly right); any other error stays on the list instead of dumping the player on a dead play screen.

nodes.label: connectSse (ticket exchange)
nodes.rationale: POSTs /api/sse-ticket with the normal credential header and spends the one-shot ticket on the stream URL, so no long-lived secret ever appears in a query string; falls back to ?pin= so an older server still yields a working stream.

nodes.label: scheduleSseReconnect (client-owned backoff)
nodes.rationale: EventSource's built-in retry re-requests the SAME url, and the ticket in it is single-use -- after the first drop its automatic retries would 401 forever and the stream would be quietly dead. Each attempt must fetch a fresh ticket, so the source is closed and reopened with a growing backoff.

nodes.label: appendFeedEntry
nodes.rationale: Player entries render as an in-world prompt line ('» did X') rather than a chat bubble; the drop-cap is suppressed whenever an entry doesn't open on an actual letter, so a scene divider or stray markdown character isn't blown up into a giant glyph.

nodes.label: appendInlineMarkup (safe inline markdown)
nodes.rationale: Models narrate in light markdown whether asked or not, so *emphasis* must render rather than print asterisks. Built from real DOM nodes, never innerHTML, so narration can never inject markup; `_underscore_` is deliberately unsupported because snake_case item names would false-positive into italics.

nodes.label: autoScroll / isNearBottom
nodes.rationale: The feed only auto-scrolls when the reader was already within 100px of the bottom; a player's own action and the first token of a fresh stream force it.

nodes.label: renderDrawer (character sheet panel)
nodes.rationale: Content is kept current even while collapsed, because on desktop the same markup is a persistent sidebar forced visible by CSS rather than a phone drawer the player taps open.

nodes.label: renderInputState (Act/Stop/thinking row)
nodes.rationale: Stop replaces Send only once the DM turn is actually under way; while a roll card is up Stop is hidden entirely, mirroring the TUI rule that Esc must never interrupt a pending roll.

nodes.label: renderSuggestions (action chips)
nodes.rationale: Tapping a chip PUTS IT IN THE INPUT rather than submitting it, so a suggestion is an editable starting point -- the goal is breaking the blank-page freeze, not turning the game into a menu. A dismiss button turns them off for good via localStorage.

nodes.label: flushLedgerToast (loot/XP toast)
nodes.rationale: Ledger deltas accumulate silently while the turn is in flight and render as one combined 'YOU GAINED' entry when busy goes false, so a turn's gains arrive as a single beat instead of a stream of fragments.

nodes.label: renderRollSheet (dice bottom sheet)
nodes.rationale: A roll is the one moment the game takes the wheel, so it gets a modal sheet over the journal; nat 20 / nat 1 recolour the die and add a flourish, and the DM-authored reason stays in its own unpredictable-length block.

nodes.label: onRollTap (spin + POST race)
nodes.rationale: Promise.all of a minimum 1.3s spin and the confirm POST gives the reveal weight; reduced-motion collapses the wait to 150ms.

nodes.label: showRevealed / auto-dismiss
nodes.rationale: The server broadcasts roll:null synchronously while resolving, which can race the POST response carrying the reveal; the dismiss is therefore scheduled from whichever side learns last, so the sheet is never yanked away before the player can read the result.

nodes.label: d20Svg (true 3D icosahedron)
nodes.rationale: Each of 20 facets is placed by a fully solved orthonormal basis (u, v, n) plus centroid, because aiming +Z at the outward normal alone leaves the roll about that normal unconstrained -- which is why an earlier rotateY/rotateX version scattered the triangles into a shard pile. A 13th baked Lambertian term shades each face for a fixed upper-left key light so the silhouette reads as a solid.

nodes.label: Web creation/retire wizard (4 dense steps)
nodes.rationale: Four dense steps, not nine sparse ones: every step used to be a single question alone on a full screen, so making a character was nine clicks before any fiction happened. The review is folded into whichever step is last (which differs between new and retire mode) so no step exists purely to confirm.

nodes.label: renderStepAbilities (assign scores)
nodes.rationale: Standard-array and rolled pools are kept side by side with their own assignments so switching tabs never loses the other; picking a value already used swaps the two positions instead of duplicating it.

nodes.label: baseStatArray (what gets POSTed)
nodes.rationale: Sends the player's BASE assignment in STAT_ORDER because the server applies the racial bonus itself in buildCharacter; sending post-bonus numbers would double them.

nodes.label: displayFinalStats (post-race preview)
nodes.rationale: Display only. The old wizard printed the base pool under a heading that said 'Final', so an Elf who would really begin at DEX 17 was shown 15 on both the stats step and the review, then saw 17 in the HUD one screen later.

hyperedges.label: Pending-roll flow: prompt, tap/SPACE, reveal, luck decision
Slash commands: shared formatters, two dispatchers, two system-entry sinks
Character creation / retire: one preset catalog, two wizards, one save path
